open_points.subject: sandbox scratch-limit detection
open_points.text: Only that error is a scratch hit
open_points.question: How does the sandbox reliably record a scratch hit when agent code catches the write error and returns normally, so that `execute_function` can still report `resource_exhausted`?
options: The in-sandbox runner reports every qualifying failed operation to the parent before control returns to agent code
Only an uncaught qualifying error or process termination counts as a scratch hit
The parent infers a hit from the resulting file size or another post-execution observation
open_points.default_guess: Have the runner report every qualifying failure to the parent immediately, including failures caught by agent code.

open_points.subject: sandbox scratch-limit classification
open_points.text: the write fails with an error the code can see ... Only that error is a scratch hit
open_points.question: What exact operation result identifies a scratch-limit hit, and how is it distinguished from host-storage exhaustion or another ordinary I/O failure?
options: Only an `EFBIG` caused by `RLIMIT_FSIZE` is a scratch hit; `ENOSPC` and `EDQUOT` are ordinary errors
Any failed write once the file has reached the configured limit is a scratch hit
Any `EFBIG`, regardless of its provenance, is a scratch hit
open_points.default_guess: Classify `EFBIG` from an operation constrained by `RLIMIT_FSIZE` as the scratch hit, and treat `ENOSPC` or `EDQUOT` as ordinary errors.

open_points.subject: sandbox file-size signal handling
open_points.text: the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it ... Code that restores the signal's default and is killed by it exited abnormally (`crashed`)
open_points.question: Which signal must the runner ignore, when must that disposition be installed, and must it remain inherited by all agent-created processes unless agent code changes it?
options: Ignore `SIGXFSZ` before loading code and let all descendants inherit that disposition
Ignore whatever signal the platform reports for the configured file-size limit
Apply the disposition only in the process that directly calls `run`
open_points.default_guess: Ignore `SIGXFSZ` before loading the module and let descendants inherit it.

open_points.subject: scope of ordinary host-storage failures
open_points.text: a write that fails because host storage is exhausted is an ordinary raised error (`crashed` if it escapes `run`)
open_points.question: Does this rule cover only agent-code writes to the exchange directory, or also runner setup/channel writes and kernel writes outside the sandbox?
options: Only agent-code writes to the exchange directory; runner or kernel I/O failures remain internal errors
All writes performed by the in-sandbox runner, including setup and result-channel writes
Every write involved in the execution, including parent and store writes
open_points.default_guess: Apply it only to agent-code writes in the exchange directory; treat runner, parent, and store I/O failures under their existing internal-error rules.
